status: v3 stack deployed on Arc testnet on 2026-11-19 (deployments.v3.testnet.json); the live site and enclaves switch to it after the UBC submission (2026-11-20): this product's enclaves register on v3 then, with their v3 compose (measured env pointing to the v3 contracts); the manifest is then updated on-chain (proposeUpdateWithURI)
summary: OpenAI-compatible chat completions. The prompt is encrypted to the enclave's X25519 key (HPKE); the enclave calls the model and signs an EIP-712 receipt per answer; the client pays from a prepaid session locked to that enclave.

modelAttestation.provider: RedPill private AI gateway (Attested Confidential Inference), verified by the enclave with @phala/aci-verifier 0.11.0 (Apache-2.0)
modelAttestation.checks: at start and every 30 min with a fresh nonce: the gateway's Intel TDX quote to Intel's root (dcap-qvl), its workload keyset bound to the quote for our nonce, keys not expired, its docker-compose measured into RTMR3 (event log replayed), and - ArcHive's own check - its OS image is the PRODUCTION dstack image (os-image-hash in RTMR3: 8db40cb23008d6213668b5816702d100b37b859a8a5bfd18d938ae3a1b3715bd)
modelAttestation.channel: every model call goes over TLS pinned to the gateway's attested key (SPKI in the keyset)
modelAttestation.serving: every answer must carry a gateway receipt citing a verified upstream session (requireVerified, requireReceipt): gpt-oss-120b is served by Tinfoil in a GPU enclave
modelAttestation.failClosed: if the gateway cannot be verified, the enclave does not start; if a call cannot be verified, no receipt is signed

settlement: SessionPay 0x606c379cd8758E3562e7ECC9972d0feF693F0763 (Arc testnet): cumulative receipts, one settle pays everything so far
tee: Intel TDX confidential VM (dstack) on Phala Cloud
verifiedOnArc: Intel's signature on each TDX quote is checked on-chain by Automata DCAP: TdxAttestationModule 0x3275fA3b519FAD912eA4a5e75Bf5078Def29D491 -> AutomataDcapAttestationFee 0x48640f7d94dE64b13c89686F3d1240A31Aeb4dc9
imageFingerprint: the registry replays the dstack RTMR3 event log on-chain (SHA-384), requires it to reproduce the quote's RTMR3, and allows the image by keccak256(MRTD | RTMR0 | RTMR1 | RTMR2 | compose-hash | os-image-hash | XFAM | TDATTRIBUTES) - no instance id, so a restart keeps the same fingerprint
reportData: REPORTDATA[0:32] binds chain id, registry, product id, operator, enclave signer and X25519 key; REPORTDATA[32:64] is a recent block hash (EIP-2935)
